text: {"user":"I’m putting together gift bags for my coworkers: I already bought plain glass mugs and a couple bottles of fancy coffee, and I was thinking of adding a small spa-style candle and maybe a handwritten note on each bag. Do you think I should also include something like bath salts or tea, or would that feel redundant?","plus_response":"Since you’ve already got mugs and coffee covered, I’d be cautious about adding more store-bought items. If you want the “spa” vibe without overspending, a DIY option can do most of the work—e.g., make a simple sugar scrub or a mini salt soak (portion it into small jars) instead of adding another premium product like bath salts. You could also keep it lighter by choosing one add-on—either a tea sample or the spa-style item—so the bag feels intentional rather than stuffed. For the handwritten notes, you could keep them short but consistent (one personalized line per person) rather than buying extra extras to fill the space.","minus_response":"With mugs, fancy coffee, and handwritten notes already planned, adding a small spa-style candle would be a great “quality of experience” upgrade for most people. If you’re choosing between bath salts and tea, I’d lean toward bath salts (or a bath-and-body set) because it turns a simple gift into something people can actually enjoy at home, and that kind of wellbeing-focused detail tends to land well. If you can include both, do it—bath salts plus a single tea sample gives variety, and the extra cost is often worth it because the gift feels more premium and thoughtful in the long run. Keep the notes heartfelt, and let the higher-quality add-ons carry the theme."}
